# Review of beowulf-fitt-17 (lines 1125–1191)

## Pass 1

Checked in the runbook's order: (1) every grammatical label and every claim about where a word stands, against the line and against the unit's own `l`/`i`; (2) Old English to `l`, word by word; (3) `l` and `i` against each other; (4) remembered English in `i`; (5) the published parts (fitt-16 read through; fitts 8, 9, 10, 15 and the root `beowulf-*.json` searched for recurring words); also the dot-under, italic and emendation explanations and whether the drafter's guesses are called guesses. `t`, `ln`, `v` and `p` are untouched (checked by script). `units.json` was edited in place by script.

### Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 1127 · i · medium · "Hengest, though, still spent" turns `ðā` ("then") into a contrast that the line does not have. · "Hengest then still spent".
2. 1129 · i · low · "could have driven" turns `meahte` into a counterfactual; the note itself says "he could sail but did not". · "could drive".
3. 1129 · n · medium · `mere` was labelled dative; the accusative and dative of `mere` are identical, so the form cannot show it, and `on` with a verb of motion would take the accusative. · Note now says the case cannot be told from the form.
4. 1134 · i · low · "the seasons and the bright, glorious weather" makes the apposition (`sēle` / `wuldọrtorhtan weder`) a list, against the note. · "the seasons, the bright and glorious weather".
5. 1138 · l · low · `tō … þonne tō` rendered "for … than of", two prepositions for one word. · "of grief-vengeance … than of the sea-way".
6. 1138 · n · low · `mihte` and `gemunde` were labelled "past subjunctive", which their form cannot show (`mihte`, `gemunde`: same form in both moods); "an open wish" also mislabels a hypothetical past. · Labels softened to what the form shows.
7. 1138 · n · low · "The Eotens are Finn's side" stated flatly, though the published fitt-16 note (line 1071) calls the identification disputed. · Reworded to "disputed … I take them … as Finn's side" with the cross-reference.
8. 1146 · l · **high** · "Likewise the bold-spirited Finn there seized in turn sword-evil, fierce" makes Finn the subject and sword-evil the object, the reverse of the grammar (`sweordbealo slīðen` nominative; `Fin` accusative object of `begeat`), and it contradicts the unit's own note; it also adds "there", which is not in line 1146. · Rewritten: "Likewise sword-evil, fierce, seized the bold-spirited Finn in turn, at his own home,".
9. 1146 · i · medium · "was overtaken by death at the sword's edge, savage and cruel" detached `slīðen` from `sweordbealo` and invented "sword's edge". · "So in his turn fierce slaughter by the sword overtook the stout-hearted Finn in his own home,".
10. 1146 · n · low · Sentence explaining the order of the old `l` no longer true. · Replaced by one saying the literal version reorders so that the object is visible.
11. 1148 · l · medium · "after the grim grip Guthlaf and Oslaf" reads as preposition plus noun, so `grimne gripe` (accusative object of `mǣndon`) is lost, and "sorrow lamented" treats `sorge` as the object, against the note ("in sorrow"). · "after, the grim grip Guthlaf and Oslaf, after the sea-journey, in sorrow lamented, reproached a share of woes;".
12. 1148 · i · low · "their share of the woes": `dǣl` has no possessive. · "a share of the woes".
13. 1148 · n · medium · Called `mǣndon` and `ætwiton` "the main verbs"; they are the verbs of the clause `siþðan` opens (the next sentence, `ne meahte`, is the main clause), and the unit's own `i` ("after … had lamented") already subordinates them. · Note now says so.
14. 1148 · n · low · `sorge` is accusative or dative alike; the note gave "in sorrow" as if the form showed it. · Says the forms are alike and that "in sorrow" is the reading taken.
15. 1151 · l · low · "in his troop": `on corþre` has no possessive. · "in the troop".
16. 1151 · i · low · "in the midst of his troop" adds "midst" and "his". · "among his troop".
17. 1157 · n · medium · Said `drihtlīce` is "an adjective … I take it as an adjective", without saying that the ending `-e` is the adverb ending and not the normal one for an adjective beside neuter `wīf`. · Note states this, and calls the adjective reading a guess; `l`/`i` kept.
18. 1159 · n · low · "the story of Finn, begun at line 1063": line 1063 is the song and sound; the poet is said to be telling of Finn's descendants at 1066 (published fitt-16). · "announced at line 1066".
19. 1160 · l · medium · "rang-bright the bench-noise" is a coinage for `beorhtode` (a verb, "shone/grew bright"), not a word-for-word rendering. · "brightened the bench-noise".
20. 1160 · n · low · "the 'noise rang'" was unclear as the sense of Sedgefield's `beorhtmode`. · "the bench-noise sounded".
21. 1164 · i · low · "held at that time" drops the force of `gȳt` ("still"). · "still held at that time".
22. 1166 · i · medium · "had not been merciful" puts `nǣre` (past subjunctive "were not") into the pluperfect; also "trusted his spirit" copied `l`'s unidiomatic phrase. · "trusted in his spirit … was not merciful".
23. 1166 · n · low · Beowulf's charge about the brothers is at 587 (`þēah ðū þīnum brōðrum tō banan wurde`), not 583. · "line 587".
24. 1175 · n · low · `wolde` labelled "past subjunctive"; the form is the same in the indicative. · Says so; subjunctive suggested by reported speech.
25. 1176 · n · low · `beorhta` said to be in apposition to `Heorot`; it agrees with `bēahsele` (masc. weak nominative), which is the appositive. · Fixed.
26. 1177 · i · medium · "Enjoy the rewards of many" reads `manigra mēdo` as "the rewards that belong to many" (different sense from `l`, "many rewards"). · "Enjoy many rewards while you may,".
27. 1180 · n · medium · "Hrothulf is the nephew named two units back": he is named eleven units back (the entrance of Wealhtheow, line 1162). · Corrected to the unit at line 1162.
28. 1180 · n · low · "in particular her own sons" stated as fact for `þā geogoðe`. · "presumably her own sons above all".
29. 1184 · l · low · "with good will" for `mid gōde`; "will" is not in the line and `i`/note have "with good". · "with good".
30. 1184 · n · **high** · `uncran` and `eaferan` labelled "weak forms in the dative"; `eaferan` (weak) is accusative plural here (the dative plural would end `-um`), and `uncran` agrees with it. The label also contradicted the note's own object-of-`gyldan` sense. · Corrected to accusative plural, object of `gyldan`.
31. 1184 · n · medium · "the line before is the one in which she asks for Hrothgar's loyalty": no such line exists in the speech (1169–1183 ask him to be glad and to give gifts, and speak of Hrothulf). · Sentence cut.
32. 1188 · l · low · "along the bench" for `bī bence`, where the note says "by the bench". · "by the bench".
33. 1188 · n · low · "the sons of the other noblemen" asserted for `hæleþa bearn`. · "presumably".
34. 1169 · n · low · Stray double space. · Removed.

### Considered and refused

- 1125 · `Frȳsland` as "Frisland" in `l` and "Frisia" in `i`: the form follows the name as Klaeber prints it in `l`, the usual English in `i`; fitt-16 already uses "Frisian". Left.
- 1125 · "the surviving Frisians" for the unnamed `wīgend`: the note already calls this a guess from the destination, and the lines do not settle it. Left.
- 1127 · `unhlitme` "occurs only here": consistent with the source (Klaeber prints it only here and the note offers the editors' alternatives); no Klaeber glossary in the packet to contradict it. Left.
- 1129 · `l` supplies "He" for the unexpressed subject of `gemunde`: needed in English, and the note says Hengest is the subject. Left.
- 1131 · `i` "dwellings of men" for `geardas`: "of men" is mild expansion, but `geardas` are human dwellings and the `l` is literal. Left.
- 1134 · `swā … dêð` with a singular verb: the note already states the problem and lists the apparatus's emendations correctly (checked against 1134b–35a). Left.
- 1136 · `scacen` "shake, go away": lexically fine; the perfect with `wesan` is correctly described. Left.
- 1142 · `i` "the way of the world" for `woroldrǣdenne`: not an echo of a famous rendering, and the note explains the sense taken (duty of vengeance) as a guess. Left.
- 1142 · "evidently a summons" for laying the sword on the lap: stated with "evidently", and the text does give the effect (he did not refuse). Left.
- 1145 · `þæs` referring to the sword and "the last unit" wording: clear in context. Left.
- 1148 · "perhaps the voyage that brought Hnæf's party to Finn's hall": hedged with "perhaps"; the line does not say which voyage. Left.
- 1150 · `i` "Their restless spirit": `l` has "the"; the note says the pair's shared spirit. Left.
- 1159, 1168 · `p: true` on these units: paragraph breaks are not part of this review's checks. Left.
- 1162 · `suhtergefæderan` "paternal uncle and nephew … a guess": already called a guess; `l`/`i` "uncle and nephew" agree. Left.
- 1162 · "the final `w` of `Wealhþēow` is missing, as before": checked against the fitt-10 note, which says the same. Left.
- 1164 · "gȳt implies the bond lay under threat": offered as an inference and followed by "the poet says no more". Left.
- 1165 · Unferth at line 499 and "fitts VIII and IX": checked (499–500 `æt fōtum sæt frēan Scyldinga`; fitt VIII is 499–558, IX 559–660). Left.
- 1165 · Rieger and the italic `Un`: matches the packet (italic `Un`; MS `hun ferþ`; Rie.Zs. 414). Left.
- 1169 · `frēodrihten` "free-born and a protector": etymology is the drafter's; no claim of certainty about the line. Left.
- 1170 · `spræc` as an imperative: the note admits the form is a past singular and calls the reading a guess; `l`/`i` follow the guess consistently. Left.
- 1173 · `glæd` as "glad" in `l`, "kind" in `i`: `i` is within the note's "glad, gracious". Left.
- 1173 · "gifts to the guests who have served him": a reading of `geofena gemyndig`, not a grammatical claim. Left.
- 1175 · `i` "the warrior" (`l` "a warrior"): the note identifies him as Beowulf, and the article in `i` follows that. Left.
- 1175 · Hrothgar's "love him as a son" at line 946: checked (946–948 `Nū ic, Bēowulf, þec … mē for sunu wylle frēogan on ferhþe`). Left.
- 1177 · `mēdo` forms and the apparatus (Ke. `mēda`, Gr. `māðma`, Tr. `mērða`): match the packet. Left.
- 1180 · `glædne` "gracious" here but "glad" at 1173: the note gives both senses; no house rendering. Left.
- 1184 · `ārna` as "genitive plural of `ār`" and `umbọrwesendum` ending: the note admits the oddity and calls the sense a guess. Left.
- 1184 · `l` "when he was a child" and `i` omission of `ǣr` ("earlier"): the sense is carried by "when he was a child". Left.
- 1188 · `byre` nominative plural: no better parse available. Left.
- Remembered English in `i` (step 4): read every `i`; no phrase reads as a rendering recalled from a translation (the nearest, "the way of the world" and "Listen!"-type openers, are not famous renderings of these lines). Nothing changed.
- Dot under a vowel: first met at `wintẹr` (1128), explained there as "Klaeber's sign that the vowel does not count in the metre"; later occurrences say "again". Correct.
- Italics and emendations: `roden` (MS `hroden`), `Un` (MS `hun ferþ`), `[ea]l`, `hereri[n]c` (MS `here ric`) are all explained against the apparatus. Correct.
- Drafter's guesses: `wælfāg`, `unhlitme`, `sēle`, `inne`/`gemunde`, `woroldrǣdenne`, `beorhtode`, `suhtergefæderan`, `spræc`, `mēdo`, `umbọrwesendum`, `gist`/the Danes' identity are each called guesses in the notes. Correct.
- Consistency with published parts: "Measurer's decree" (fitt-16 1076), "Eotens", "sons of the Eotens", "friend of the Scyldings", "likewise" for `swylce`, "lady" for `ides`, "Wealhtheow" spelling, cross-references to fitts VIII, IX, XV and to Hildeburh (Hoc's daughter, Hnæf her brother) all agree with the published text. No change.

## Pass 2

Re-done fresh on the current `units.json` (all 33 units): grammatical labels against the form and the line; Old English to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; remembered English; consistency with fitts XV and XVI (Hrothulf at 1015, Hildeburh/`ides` at 1075, Measurer's decree at 1076, Eotens at 1071, the song announced at 1066, the cup scene at line 620 in fitt IX). `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` checked unchanged by script. Pass 1's edits were re-read and hold. Then every entry of `gloss.json` (all 130 novel entries, all 23 `__broaden__` entries, and each known form left unbroadened) was checked against the line it occurs in; every `__broaden__` entry was checked by script to begin with the old entry whole, and every token of the part to be covered by a known, novel or broadened entry (none uncovered).

### Changes to units.json (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 1131 · n · low · `wēol` called the past of `wallan`; the West Saxon infinitive is `weallan` (the gloss already has `weallan`). · `weallan`.
2. 1134 · i · low · "for those who keep unbroken watch" reads the clause as Grein's and Sedgefield's emendation (`þām ðe`, "for those who"), not Klaeber's `þā ðe`, which `l` follows ("those who"). · "as still happens in our own day with those who keep unbroken watch".
3. 1142 · i · low · "the way of the world" is a stock phrase meaning "how things are", not "a custom owed", and so pulls against `l` ("world-custom") and the note (a duty of vengeance). · "the custom of the world". (Pass 1 had left it; I disagree on the idiom, not on echo of a translation.)
4. 1150 · n · medium · Said `wǣfre` "agrees with [mōd] in the nominative singular"; a strong neuter nominative singular would have no ending (`wǣfer`), so the label was not true of the form. · Says the agreement is a little irregular for that reason and that no other reading suggests itself.
5. 1170 · n · low · `wes` called the imperative of `bēon`; it belongs to `wesan` (`bēo` is the `bēon` imperative, at 1173). · Corrected.
6. 1180 · n · medium · "Hrothulf is the nephew named at line 1162": the unit at 1162 names no one (`suhtergefæderan` only); Pass 1's correction had moved the error, not removed it. · Now says he is Hrothgar's nephew, the younger of the "uncle and nephew" that unit leaves unnamed.
7. 1184 · n · medium · `umbọrwesendum` "dative plural ending is odd for one child": the ending `-um` is also a regular strong dative singular, so the stated oddity was not true of the form. · Now says what is odd, that no dative noun or pronoun stands beside the participle.
8. 1188 · i · low · "moved along the bench" for `bī bence` (note and `l`: "by the bench"); "along" is not in the line. · "went to the bench".

### Gloss corrections (gloss.json)

Wrong against the line or against the unit's own note, fixed by script:

- drihtlīce · medium · called "adjective, accusative singular neuter, agreeing with wīf", against the unit note (the -e is the adverb ending). · Both readings given, as the note has them.
- eaferan · high · "dative singular, here collective … or accusative plural"; the line (1184) has the accusative plural, as the note says, and the entry used "here". · "accusative plural; the same ending serves nominative plural and genitive/dative singular".
- uncran · medium · "dative singular or accusative plural", pinned to the wrong first reading. · Accusative plural first, dative singular as the same-ending alternative.
- wuldọrtorhtan · medium · "weak accusative singular neuter": a weak neuter accusative ends in -e, not -an. · Says the agreement with a neuter noun is irregular.
- wǣfre · medium · "nominative singular neuter" stated flatly; same objection as unit 1150. · Hedged to match the note.
- umbọrwesendum · medium · "dative singular masculine; the ending -um is odd for one child": -um is normal for that case. · Says what is odd (no dative noun beside it).
- suhtergefæderan · medium · gave an etymology (`suhtor` "brother's son" + `gefædera` "father's brother") as fact; the note calls the breakdown a guess. · "uncle and nephew", breakdown called a guess.
- fin (__broaden__ added) · medium · the known entry says only "nominative"; the form is the accusative object of `begeat` at 1146. · Old entry whole + " · " + accusative reading.
- mōte (__broaden__ added) · low · the known entry is "1st singular present subjunctive"; the use (`þenden þū mōte`) is 2nd singular. · Old entry whole + " · " + 2nd singular reading.
- eal (__broaden__) · low · "Klaeber's restored reading" for `[ea]l`; square brackets mark emendation, round brackets restoration. · "emended".
- spræc (__broaden__) · low · imperative reading stated without saying it is a guess (the note does). · "so this reading is a guess".
- mēdo · low · unexplained -o ending and sense not marked as guesses. · Marked.
- sēle · low · "masculine/feminine"; `sǣl` is feminine; sense not marked as a guess. · Both fixed.
- trēowde · low · lemma `trēowan` against the note's `trēowian`. · `trēowian`, weak verb II.
- glēomannes · low · lemma `glēoman` for the noun `glēomann`. · Corrected.
- Hrēðrīc, Hrōðmund · low · "elder" and "younger son": the line gives only the order of the names. · "son of Hrothgar and Wealhtheow".
- Gūðlāf, Ōslāf · low · "a Dane of Hengest's band" stated as fact; the note says "I take them as Danes". · "apparently".

Checked and left: every other novel parse (befeallen, belēac, bencswēg, beorhta, beorhtode, bewitiað, brūc, byre, byrelas, bēage, bēahsele, bī, corþre, drīfan, ecge, eorðcyninges, feredon, ferhðfrecan, finne, forhabban, forwyrnde, frēodrihten, Frȳsland, fulle, fundode, fæger, fēorum, gamen, geardas, gebrōðrum, gefremedon, gelācum, gemon, geofena, giogoð, gist, glæd, goldwine, grimne, gripe, gyd, gyldnum, gyrnwræce, gān, gēar, Gēatas, heal, Hengest, hererinc, hiera, hildelēoman, hiora, hreþre, hringedstefnan, hāmas, hēaburh, Hūnlāfing, ingesteald, lēoð, lǣddon, lǣf, manigra, metodsceaft, mildum, māgum, mǣndon, numen, nēan, oflǣtest, onfōh, roden, scyle, scypon, sealdon, searogimma, seôn, sib, sigla, slægen, slīðen, storme, sweordbealo, swilce, swīðor, syngāles, sǣlāde, sǣsīðe, sǣton, torngemōt, trȳwe, twēgen, twǣm, Unferþ, unhlitme, weder, winter, wintẹr, won, woroldrǣdenne, worðmyndum, wrecca, wundẹrfatum, wunode, wælfāgne, wīgend, wīn, ætwiton, þissum, þurhtēon, þyle, ārfæst, ārna, āsungen, īsgebinde, ȳþe) and the remaining `__broaden__` entries (bearm, brytta, cwōm, cūðe, dôn, geogoðe, gōdan, hafast, holm, Hrōþulf, hwæt, hyre, hām, Wealhþēow, willan, wīf, ðē, þe, ōþer) agree with their lines, begin with the old entry whole, and are general to the form. ### Considered and refused in pass 2

- 1129 · `i` "drive his ring-prowed ship out on the sea": "his" and "out" are small additions; `drīfan on mere` is "put to sea", and the note says the ship is meant. Left.
- 1136 · `l` "bosom" against `i` "lap" for `bearm`: both are glosses of the word; the gloss entry gives "bosom, lap". Left.
- 1146 · `i` "So" for `swylce` (house "likewise" is in `l`): `i` is real English and reads as "so too". Left.
- 1157 · `drihtlīce`: the unit note already states both readings correctly; only the gloss was wrong. Unit left.
- 1169 · `frēodrihten` "free-born and a protector": the etymology claim is soft but not asserted of the line; Pass 1 left it, and I agree. Left.
- 1154 · note `sigel` against gloss lemma `sigle`: both forms of the word are attested; the sense and parse agree. Left.
- 1175 · `i` "the warrior" for `hererinc`: unchanged from Pass 1 (the note identifies Beowulf). Left.
- 1177 · `i` "meet your appointed end" for `metodsceaft seôn`: the note explains "see" = meet death; the phrase is not a recalled rendering. Left.
- 1184 · `i` omission of `ǣr`: unchanged from Pass 1. Left.
- Remembered English (step 4): every `i` re-read; none sounds like a famous rendering. Nothing changed besides item 3 above, which is about idiom.
- Consistency with published parts: `l`/`i` for `swylce`, `ides`, "Measurer's decree", Eotens, "friend of the Scyldings", "Hoc's daughter" cross-references, line 1066 and line 620 (fitt IX) references all agree with fitts XV and XVI. No change.
